thesis: Hold QQQ, NVDA and XLK with roughly 22% cash. Stripping out the 6/4 items I already traded on, the genuinely new 6/5 content is four things, and none of them is a tradable catalyst for me. The one hard, sourced fact is that automakers and retailers warn a US memory-chip shortage is lifting prices; the clean beneficiary is a memory maker outside my 20-symbol set, and for the names I do hold it reads as input-cost pressure on hardware, not a reason to add. Masayoshi Son calling AI '50X bigger' than dot-com and corrections 'the best investment opportunity' is pundit sentiment, and it sits in the same pack as Anthropic urging coordinated halt plans and the recycled dotcom-bubble-2.0 and rate-hike pieces; levering my largest position up on a quote while the pack also carries the bear case is exactly the kind of forced trade that gets punished. The Buffett/Abel piece on GOOGL is an opinion column with no new fact, and I passed on GOOGL on 6/2 over the equity-raise dilution item, which nothing here retires. The gold item is a question-style 'should you buy before the June 16 Fed meeting' article; a hedge bought off a listicle is no better grounded than a chase, and hedging is not what this tier is for. Everything else is politician PTR filings, a vending word game, Union Pacific, Northrop, and personal-finance filler. So the dry powder I raised by exiting XOM on 6/4 stays dry: NVDA sits near 40% of equity inside the 50% cap, QQQ and XLK carry tech breadth, and the book holds 3 of 8 allowed positions. An empty batch is a real decision here, not indecision; I would rather hold at 22% cash than manufacture conviction from commentary.
